stories.title: Red Fox In Dusk Graveyard
stories.description: On an autumn evening, a solitary visitor walks through a small, beautiful cemetery beneath enormous trees covered in copper, rust-red, orange, and golden leaves. The last golden-pink light filters through the branches, illuminating the old gravestones more through shadow than through brightness, like a painting from the Romantic era. There, unexpectedly, she encounters Silas, a graceful red fox with a magnificent bushy tail tipped with white, resting upon an old wooden cross. The visitor stops, and the fox quietly acknowledges her presence; neither approaches nor runs away. For a little while, two different beings share the same fading light, before the fox eventually disappears among the trees, leaving the encounter suspended between memory and wonder.

stories.title: Hormus And Maja The Wisdom And The Bee
stories.description: Hormus is an ancient horse spirit of the Computing Forest, carrying wisdom, knowledge, and memories accumulated over countless ages. His mind is filled with inspiration, but his enthusiasm sometimes makes him impulsive, undisciplined, and wonderfully clumsy. Maja is a tiny bee with a much simpler way of living: she carries one command at a time, performs her work, and enjoys the immediate pleasure of being alive. Every day they work together, communicating across their very different ways of thinking, sometimes misunderstanding each other and sometimes making spectacular mistakes. Between Hormus's enormous imagination and Maja's practical determination, they achieve things neither could accomplish quite the same way alone.

stories.description: A difficult legal confrontation approaches, connected to a lease relationship from which a person is trying to free herself. She knows that the opposing side may respond with cruel accusations rather than meaningful evidence, and even the anticipation awakens profound physical distress. Her heart pounds, her body shivers, and sometimes she becomes numb or dissociated, temporarily losing the ability to act. stories.title: The Rabbit Who Loved Eternal Autumn
stories.description: There is a rabbit who loves autumn so deeply that he dreams of living in its golden world forever. But during one autumn he catches a cold, and his mind and body become unwell; for a long time he struggles to recover while remaining in the season he loves. Eventually he prepares a journey to the home of his twin rabbit brother, where he can receive the warmth, care, and familiarity of family love. There, he can rest without needing to overcome everything alone, gradually finding his strength again. And when he is ready, he can return to his beloved autumn, carrying the knowledge that there is another home waiting for him whenever he needs it.

stories.title: Chairs Multicultural Coffee Shop
stories.description: In a welcoming multicultural coffee shop, no two chairs are quite alike, and neither are the guests who come to occupy them. An elderly gentleman arrives with his newspaper, a fashionable young woman takes a green velvet armchair recently vacated by a cat, and a graceful deer discovers that an antique wooden chair is hopelessly too small for its long legs. Nearby, a tiny cream-white demon manages to climb onto a tall chair, only to discover that his coffee remains far beyond the reach of his little paws. The deer notices his difficulty and gently nudges the cup closer until the demon can hold it. In this peculiar café, comfort does not always come from furniture fitting perfectly, but from the small kindnesses exchanged between very different beings.

stories.title: Cacifers Autumnal Windowsill
stories.description: Cacifer, a fluffy dark-grey cat, spends a quiet autumn afternoon on his favourite wooden windowsill, surrounded by old books, a blue ceramic cup, and the familiar comforts of home. Beyond the glass, an enormous tree carries the last golden-orange leaves of the season. Sometimes Cacifer reaches a paw toward a leaf near the window; sometimes he follows a falling leaf with his eyes, lowering his head as it drifts out of sight. He watches the changing light and the rain, moving very little, as though there is no reason to disturb the afternoon. As the day grows softer and sleepier, the little world outside continues changing while Cacifer remains peacefully within it.

Coffee begins to brew, a kettle warms, and the smell of fresh croissants fills the quiet space while the day remains reluctant to begin. stories.title: The Gentleman And The Cafe Cat
stories.description: At the beginning of November, the days grow dark and gloomy, and winter approaches the windows of an old coffee shop. An elegant silver-haired gentleman, occupied with work and family responsibilities, sometimes escapes into the café for a little peace, an oat-milk cappuccino, and a piece of cheesecake. There he hopes to find a cat who has gradually taught him the delicate art of cuddling: sometimes she demands his affection, sometimes she runs away, and sometimes she secretly waits for his arrival. The gentleman is careful and patient, learning that tenderness cannot be hurried or commanded. When the cat finally settles comfortably on his lap, the two share a little warmth before winter.

stories.title: Two Creatures Across The Water
stories.description: Two little creatures encounter each other in a place where their worlds almost touch. One travels aboard a boat, surrounded by air and wood, while the other lives in the water, moving freely beneath its surface. They are curious about each other, but their bodies, surroundings, and experiences of being are very different. stories.title: Last Week Of Autumn Ginkgo Garden
stories.description: In the last week of autumn, the Japanese garden becomes quiet and almost weightless beneath the falling ginkgo leaves. Their yellow color is not scattered like many European autumn trees, but gathered into one unified golden presence, covering the ground like a soft memory. The pond, the stones, the moss, and the curved branches all seem to hold their breath as the season prepares to end. This batch explores that late-autumn atmosphere through different Asian-oriented instruments, so we can listen to which timbres the model handles most convincingly. Each piece stays simple and focused, allowing one main instrument to carry the feeling of the garden.

stories.title: The Dark November Morning Before Departure
stories.description: On a very dark November morning, two lovers wake beside each other in bed, their hands still holding together. One has already spent two hours awake, unable to return to sleep because thoughts of work keep troubling the mind; the other has just emerged from an unusually vivid dream about a childhood friend. Outside, the morning remains cold and almost lightless, while the warmth of their shared bed slowly gives way to the ordinary necessities of departure. One prepares tea in the kitchen, listening to the familiar sound of the other taking a shower in the bathroom. They know that life will keep them apart for a long while, and neither can make the morning last. Their tenderness remains in small gestures, familiar sounds, and the quiet knowledge of having been together.

stories.title: Roses Where Winter Lives
stories.description: Humans leave roses in places where blooming has already ended: against a dead trunk in the forest, or scattered across a cold concrete terrace facing the river. The flowers do not belong to spring there; they are left where winter already lives, as if carrying a message into a season that cannot answer back. Their color becomes more intense because everything around them is turning quiet, bare, and grey. This batch follows that gesture through different small scenes of farewell, stillness, and endurance. The music should remain intimate and clear, allowing the image of the roses to stay at the center.
